DXC issue #1702 -- Array as parameter of function
https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/1702

WHAT TO LOOK FOR

Three compilers, three different answers to the same input.

The construct under test is the unsized array parameter "float4 a[]".
FXC rejects it outright:

    error X3072: 'a': array dimensions of function parameters must be
    explicit

DXC accepts it and then miscompiles it. Look at the value stored:

    call void @dx.op.bufferStore.f32(..., float undef, float undef,
                                          float undef, float undef, i8 15)

The argument never reaches Func(), so undefined values are written.
DXC's own validator then rejects the module it just produced:

    error: Assignment of undefined values to UAV.
    Validation failed.

Clang compiles the same source correctly, storing float 1.0.

So whichever answer is right for the language -- reject it like FXC, or
accept it like Clang -- DXC currently matches neither.

CONTROL: give the parameter an explicit size, "float4 a[2]", and DXC
compiles cleanly and stores 1.0. The unsized parameter is the variable
under test, not array passing in general.

NOTE ON THE SHADER STAGE: the issue reports a pixel shader, and that is
what was tested locally. This is a compute restating of it, because
Clang's DXIL backend cannot lower any pixel shader writing SV_Target --
a one-line "float4 main() : SV_Target { return 0; }" fails there too --
so a ps pane would show an unrelated error and prove nothing. The pixel
version fails differently but from the same cause: the call is dropped,
main() is empty, and the only hint is "warning: Declared output
SV_Target0 not fully written in shader".

NOTE: the assert reported in the issue (SROA_Helper::RewriteBitCast)
does NOT happen in any release from v1.4.1907 (2019) onward -- the
oldest that ships a usable dxc, so when it stopped is unknown. Do not
go looking for it here; its absence does not mean the issue is fixed.
